sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美西语近岸软件研发外包与数字客服中心

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Proprietary Ultra-Low Latency Algorithmic Market Making

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Colombia (Unitary Republic; no separate sub-state commercial registrars)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Colombia–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (Investment Chapter, effective 2012)
Colombia–Canada Free Trade Agreement (Investment Chapter, effective 2011)
Colombia–Mexico–Chile Pacific Alliance Framework Agreement (Additional Protocol)
Colombia–Spain Double Taxation Avoidance Convention (LLD./1991, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 526 of 1999 (UIAF creation and financial intelligence); Law 1121 of 2006 and Law 1762 of 2015 (AML/CFT and anti-illicit finance); Decree 830 of 2021 (UBO regulation); DIAN Resolution 000164 of 2021 (Obligatory registration in the Single Registry of Ultimate Beneficial Owners – RUB); Superintendencia Financiera Circular Básica Jurídica 029 of 2014 (AML/CFT for regulated entities); Congreso de Colombia Law 1955 of 2019, Article 48 (legal mandate for UBO disclosure).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Certificate of Good Standing of corporate shareholder (if any)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Companies Registry in the country of origin (e.g., Companies House, State Secretary, Chamber of Commerce)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Colombia is a contracting party to the Hague Apostille Convention 1961)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copy of each ultimate beneficial owner and legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Consular or Notarial authority under origin country rules
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, if non-Hague state, Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney for local incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Any civil notary in country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Letter of Commitment / source of funds declaration for capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Signatory UBO or authorized officer of corporate shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of UBO Register extract (if parent is in an EU or OECD jurisdiction with a UBO registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National UBO registry of the foreign parent company’s jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, shareholders and counterparty financial institutions against (i) OFAC Specialty Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; (ii) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) EU consolidated financial sanctions list; (iv) Colombian UIAF ‘Libradores’ and thematic lists; (v) Superintendencia Financiera registry of PEPs and sanctionable persons under Circular 029/2014. Risk-based enhanced due diligence is mandatory for all non-resident UBOs and any investor using corporate vehicles registered in FATF listed high-risk jurisdictions.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) operated by the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio and the Chamber of Commerce (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be composed using the Spanish alphabet; names must be in Castilian Spanish or accepted transliteration into Latin script. Accenture-style trade names may use latin-character, non-Castilian words if they are written with Spanish-accepted letters. All official registration documents and the constitutional bye-laws must be drafted in Spanish.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Chamber of Commerce rejects the proposed name (homonymy, confusion, or use of a sensitive protected token), the applicant may file a written reconsideration petition ('recurso de reposición') with the same Chamber within 10 business days. If rejected again, a subsidiary appeal ('recurso de apelación') may be lodged before the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio within 5 business days. A fresh RUES name search must be submitted if the rejection is administrative and no active reservation exists.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially Permissible. A Colombian SAS must designate a physical office address within Colombia for legal notice purposes. Virtual office services are accepted by the Registry only if the provider offers a physical floor/location in the city of incorporation and accepts legal notifications and periodic inspections. For high-frequency trading, a co-located data center and a physical legal address are strongly advisable for exchange membership and regulatory inspections.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-High for regulated financial services. Probability approximately 35-60% within the first 18 months for entities holding any FIU-cleared trading license, foreign exchange clearing access, or portal accounts with Colombian broker-dealers. If the SAS remains a quiescent holding entity, likelihood is less than 20%.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Chamber of Commerce registration fee (matrícula mercantil) – SAS base capital USD 10,000
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per Decreto 1074 de 2015, based on formalities and flat fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and pre-registration search fee (RUES / Homologación)
Notarial deed and incorporation legalization (Escritura Pública / private document before notary)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff table (Arancel notarial) for SAS formation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and notarization of foreign UBO documents (3 documents x USD 40)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign competent authorities (e.g., Secretary of State) and Colombian Consulate if notarial
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed per-document apostille tariff by origin jurisdiction; Colombian consular tariff if required

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Local attorney / incorporation agent fees for due diligence, by-laws drafting, UBO register submission and subscription of shares
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for stage-1 corporate formation in Bogotá / Medellín

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 1258 of 2008 (Sociedades por Acciones Simplificadas), Articles 1-45; Código de Comercio Decree 410 of 1971, Articles 98-112; Superintendencia de Sociedades Circular Básica Jurídica
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá (Mercantile Registry Division, RUES platform)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (Private Incorporation Deed) authenticated before a Notary Public
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None - the S.A.S. permits zero or nominal paid-up capital; capital may remain unpaid above 25% of subscribed value; no escrow bank account is required at incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDING SHAREHOLDERS OF [COMPANY NAME] S.A.S. — Adopted on [date] by the unanimous consent of the sole/founding shareholder. WHEREAS the shareholder has subscribed and paid at least the minimum portion of the authorized share capital; and WHEREAS the registered office has been established: RESOLVED, 1. The share subscription and capital allocation in the incorporation deed are ratified; 2. The registered office is fixed at [address], Bogotá D.C., Colombia; 3. [Name] is appointed Legal Representative with full corporate powers, and [Name] Alternate Legal Representative; 4. The representatives are authorized to execute the mercantile registration before the Cámara de Comercio and tax registration before DIAN; 5. Resolution effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Private Incorporation Document
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Documento Privado de Constitución containing bylaws, share allocations, registered office address, and legal representative appointments; have the founding shareholder(s) sign in person and obtain notarial recognition of signatures (autenticación) plus fotoíntegra stamp for digital copies if required.
required_dossiers: Government-issued ID or passport of shareholder(s)
Power of attorney if a legal representative signs
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary rejects a clause, amend the deed and re-authenticate; the deed may be redrafted as a Public Deed (Escritura Pública) at later registry request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Mercantile Registration with the Chamber of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá (Virtual and in-person service window via RUES)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the authentic incorporation document through the RUES platform or the Chamber's online service module; pay the registration fee plus the Chamber incorporation fee; obtain the Registration Certificate (Certificado de Matrícula Mercantil) and the registration number.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of registration fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry files a petición, correct the observations within one month and resubmit via RUES; a second adverse decision may be challenged by a reposición recourse within 10 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN - Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (MUISCA online portal, integrated with Chamber registration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the RUT registration online through DIAN's MUISCA system using the Chamber-issued registration data; request the Número de Identificación Tributaria (NIT) and electronic signature certificate.
required_dossiers: ID and tax classification data of the legal representative
Bank evidence for the certification of the registered capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN denies the RUT, correct the discrepancies in declared economic activities or capital information and re-apply; a reconsideration request may be filed within 10 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Superintendencia de Sociedades Inspection and Municipal Alignment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Superintendencia de Sociedades (online regulatory platform) and municipal planning authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the company's annual report and undergo incorporation inspection; verify that bylaws comply with corporate governance rules under Colombian law; complete any municipal operating registration at the Office of Economic Development for the ICA tax (Industria y Comercio) census.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Superintendencia requests corrective information, resubmit with legal counsel's cover letter; appeal adverse determinations via recurso de reposición y apelación.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (SFC) and Bolsa de Valores de Colombia (BVC) for trading venue access
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorización de Funcionamiento como Inversionista/Operador de Mercados and Memorandum de Acceso a la BVC (Market-maker access agreement)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente (SDA) / Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / No Full EIA Required (low-impact office operations only)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Decreto 1076 de 2015 and Resolución 631 de 2015 for wastewater discharge; air quality limits under Resolución 2254 de 2017; electronic waste handling under Resolución 1570 de 2020 and Ley 1672 de 2013.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos - Certificado de Bomberos (fire safety compliance inspection); Secretaría de Planeación - land use certification and zoning census; structural and electrical load certification of the operational trading floor; compliance with Decreto 1072 de 2015 (SG-SST workplace health and safety); access-control clearance for high-security server rooms and emergency backup power systems.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN), operating via the MUISCA electronic portal (www.dian.gov.co); the Colombian peso foreign-exchange and export-proceeds regime is jointly administered by the Banco de la República and the Ministry of Finance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign parent establishing a Colombian S.A.S. must: (i) execute the company deeds before a notary and register the company with the Cámara de Comercio (commercial registry); (ii) file Form 0001 ('Registro Único Tributario, Actualización, Suspensión, Reactivación y Cancelación') with DIAN through the MUISCA system to obtain the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria), which is the sole statutory tax ID; (iii) simultaneously enroll in the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) and obtain an electronic-signature credential; (iv) designate a resident legal representative/apoderado and Colombian fiscal domicile for service of process; (v) inform the exchange-control intermediary (bank) and evidence the inbound foreign investment in the Banco de la República's foreign-exchange registry to legalize the capital contribution and future dividend/profit repatriation; (vi) enable DIAN-approved electronic invoicing software and file the respective IT/software enabling notice before commencing tax-relevant operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation – the S.A.S. is a Colombian tax-resident corporation subject to corporate income tax (CIT) at 35% on worldwide income (2024 rate, established under Law 2277/2022 and subsequent rules), with no pass-through or check-the-box treatment; the shareholders are separately taxable on dividends distributed, and the S.A.S. is also subject to the surtax on income and equity ('tributo de renta'). Foreign shareholders are treated as non-residents for Colombian-source income only. Territorial scope: worldwide income for residence; equity and assets worldwide are included in the net-worth base, while Colombian-source-only rules do not apply to domestic corporations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia does not operate a check-the-box regime comparable to US Subchapter S or an LLC pass-through election; the S.A.S. is mandatorily entity-level taxed. Statutory elections actually available include: (i) election to apply the 'Compañía Holding Colombiana' (CHC) regime for qualifying Colombian holding entities, which may change the taxation of foreign dividends and capital gains arising abroad; (ii) election to recognize revenue under the fiscal-IFRS alignment or the former system where applicable; (iii) election for the 'regla de valoración de activos' relating to inflation-adjusted equity; (iv) option to be a special regime ('régimen tributario especial') only for non-profit entities, not here; (v) for VAT: election to be a simple-regime taxpayer is not allowed to S.A.S. (companies are always in the common regime); (vi) anti-hybrid elections under Law 2155/2021 regarding controlled foreign company (CFC) rules and hybrid financial instrument mismatches (e.g., designation of the 'originator' approach) have limited utility for a wholly domestic trading S.A.S. and should be analyzed against the OECD MLI obligations.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto sobre las Ventas) – Colombian Value Added Tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general economic-turnover registration threshold applies to corporations: every S.A.S., once commercially registered, must enroll in the RUT and is a 'gran contribuyente' or common-regime VAT subject regardless of revenue; a de minimis sale-threshold regime (COP 4,500,000 per annual taxable sales) exists only for natural persons under the 'régimen simple de tributación – SIMPLE' but is not available to S.A.S. ownership structures. Financial market-making and ultra-low-latency trading commissions are generally classified as exempt financial services under Article 476 of the Estatuto Tributario, but all entities must still declare VAT even when only performing exempt transactions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-responsible taxpayers in Colombia are required to issue the 'factura electrónica de venta' (FEV) with DIAN real-time fiscal clearance: invoices must be generated by a DIAN-enabled software provider, digitally signed, transmitted to MUISCA, and assigned a CUFE (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica) or CUDI; the DIAN performs immediate schema validation; the supplier must also transmit the 'eventos de recepción' (acceptance/rejection) from the buyer; a printed QR-enabled PDF or XML is the operational invoice. The same obligation applies with the DIAN 'Radian' platform for electronic credit notes, debit notes, and supporting documents. Any non-compliant invoice is legally invalid and the VAT deduction/credit is denied; DIAN has authority to adopt asynchronous exchange-mode in connection failures but synchronous clearance is the default mandate. Export invoices must additionally include the customs export report reference and exchange-control data.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports: zero-rated (tarifa 0% under Articles 479-481 Estatuto Tributario) when a valid export customs declaration (DEX) is filed, the goods physically leave the national customs territory, and the seller is the exporter of record. Services exports: zero-rated only if (i) the service is rendered to a non-resident entity or to a foreign-domiciled permanent establishment of a resident, (ii) the service is effectively used/consumed abroad, and (iii) the economic benefit is realized entirely outside Colombia; for an HFT/market-making entity, fees, commissions, and ultra-low-latency data or infrastructure services provided to foreign trading venues and offshore counterparties may qualify where the 'integration into the Colombian territory' test (e.g., no local data-feed consumption, no local user) is factually met per DIAN Concepto 0341/2022 and related criteria. The zero-rating grants a right to recover the underlying 19% input VAT evidenced in invoices charged on local costs (co-location, infrastructure, consulting).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación – DEX/Form SH-731) electronically accepted by DIAN-migrated MUISCA system
Bill of Lading (B/L), Airway Bill, or multimodal transport document evidencing tangible goods exit; for services, the signed service contract and an engagement letter

Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de canalización de divisas) or the 'Declaración de Cambio' (Form 490) lodged through a local authorized brokerage entity evidencing the collection of export proceeds in hard currency
Commercial invoice/electronica invoice with CUFE, indicating the 'exportación' nature and zero-rating
Certificate of the Banco de la República or exchange-control intermediary confirming funding repatriation within the legal term
Where applicable, authority permits from the financial regulator (e.g., non-resident broker authorization or SFC foreign-exchange clearing documentation)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Colombian export zero-rating is subject to strict ex-post DIAN audit: (i) export proceeds must be repatriated (canalized) within 180 days of shipment/performance; failure to repatriate forces the taxpayer to charge the 19% VAT retroactively plus default interest (intereses moratorios) and generates an automatic correction-irregularity claim; (ii) baseless zero-rating claims trigger the monetary sanctions of Articles 653 and 673 Estatuto Tributario, ranging from 10% to 200% of the improperly obtained refund; (iii) criminal liability arises under the tax fraud offence 'obtención de devolución o compensación improcedente' (Article 647A Estatuto Tributario), punishable by imprisonment of 60-120 months; (iv) DIAN cross-matches export declarations, port/warehouse exit records, financial transactions, and FX declarations through its data-analysis and 'BEBIDA' platform; refunds are typically blocked if any inconsistency is flagged; (v) the DIAN audit window is five years from the filing deadline, extendable to ten years for unreported activities, and any discovered VAT clawback is accruable with two-year prescription from the final administrative decision.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (Central Bank of Colombia) together with the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit and the Financial Superintendence of Colombia (Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia) under the national foreign exchange control framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia operates a managed-float regime for the COP with current-account convertibility, but enforces exchange controls on capital flows through the oficial exchange market. All foreign debt, direct equity investment, and import/export proceeds of resident entities must be channeled through authorized foreign exchange intermediaries and reported on the applicable Declaración de Cambio. Profit remittances and capital repatriation are freely permitted once the foreign investment is registered with Banco de la República, subject to tax clearance from DIAN and compliance with beneficial-ownership disclosure. Hurdles include mandatory exchange registration for non-resident capital contributed to the S.A.S., segregation of eligible operations, and the requirement to obtain a mercado cambiario surveillance code.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Colombian resident exporters and service providers must channel export proceeds into the country through an authorized foreign exchange intermediary within a statutory term of six months from the date of the export bill of lading or service invoice; this term is extendable for a further six months with prior Central Bank authorization. Although the proceeds must be surrendered to the official market, there is no mandatory conversion to COP; the exporter may maintain approved foreign currency balances, but the transaction must be reported and the funds remain subject to exchange-control verification windows.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Viability rating for offshore digital EMIs as primary treasury accounts is Low. Colombian foreign-exchange regulations require legal-entity accounts held by domestically ownering commercial banks to accept incoming investment capital and effect official-market transfers. Non-resident EMIs may provide ancillary FX pricing or payment initiation, but they cannot lawfully operate a Colombian capital account, issue local accounts, or receive direct foreign investment without acquiring a Colombian financial-institution license.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Colombian financial institutions generally require the legal representative and ultimate beneficial owner to attend a personal KYC interview at a main or designated branch for a newly incorporated S.A.S., particularly when the entity's business is proprietary trading and involves low-physical-presence operations. Remote opening is possible only under a formal risk-based dossier, authenticated copies of incorporation documents, apostilled powers of attorney, and video identity verification, subject to the bank's internal risk appetite; in practice, a physical board member visit is near-mandatory for the initial account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-face-to-face algorithmic trading profile with high transaction velocity and no clear physical operations in Colombia.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide audited annual financial statements, a documented trading and market-making strategy, the proprietary-trading license and self-regulation certificate, detailed broker/counterparty list, proof of regulatory oversight in the foreign market, and a written AML/risk assessment demonstrating that the S.A.S. uses only proprietary funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex or tax-heaven jurisdiction presence in shareholder chain, causing suspicion that beneficial ownership is concealed.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit beneficial-ownership declarations under Circular 083/2022 with DIAN and Banco de la República, a full organizational chart broken down to natural persons, certified copies of passports, and notarized exhibition of share-registry records demonstrating each ultimate owner's identity and contribution source.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of treasury funds, particularly electronic transfers from e-money or financial technology platforms rather than the originating investor's bank.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present bank-to-bank statements in the name of the investor, capital-contribution agreements, proof of tax identification in the source jurisdiction, prior-year audited financials of the parent entity, and a sworn affidavit linking each wire to a genuine commercial purpose.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: A foreign investor capital injection into the Colombian S.A.S. must route by SWIFT MT103 through its home-country correspondent to the S.A.S.'s COP/USD operational account at a tier-one Colombian commercial bank. The credit must be accompanied by a Banco de la República direct-investment registration code (Declaración de Cambio No. 6) and a non-trading purposible copy of the registration certificate. The receiving bank verifies the NIT of the S.A.S., the investor's foreign-tax identification, the applied exchange rate (not greater than the market reference rate), and the absence of DIAN tax-pending certificates; the transaction is then recorded on a 'Formulario de Inversión Internacional' and the COP proceeds are available only after compliance clearance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational and trading disbursements use SWIFT MT103 for service payments, broker margin calls, exchange colocation fees, and software licensing; import-related settlements use commercial letters of credit (at-sight or usance) opened by the Colombian bank against invoices, packing lists, and exchange-control documentation. Every disbursement exceeding $2,000 USD (or the Central Bank's reporting threshold) must be channeled through an authorized foreign-exchange intermediary and declared on the corresponding 'Declaración de Cambio para Transferencias al Exterior'. Services unrelated to trading may be cleared over the same rails only after complying with DIAN withholding regimes (hourly, occasional, and financial returns) and, where applicable, submitting Form 4681.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) in USD/COP for achieved-proceeds hedging
Deliverable currency forwards (USD/COP deliverable) subject to current-account feasibility and allowance by the bank
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps between COP and USD managed in the official exchange market through an authorized intermediary
FX options whose short-leg cash settlement is reported and approved for hedging of trade payables and investment-related exposures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registry Renewal (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (local Chamber of Commerce)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January through 31 March each year, based on status as of 31 December of the preceding fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal incurs surcharges and default interest; continued failure cancels commercial registration, prohibits statutory operations, and can trigger forced judicial liquidation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax and Complementary Return (Declaración de Renta y Complementario)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN - Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in April following the calendar year-end; exact date assigned by DIAN under the NIT last-digit calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% per month or fraction, capped at 100% of assessed tax, plus statutory default interest; continued non-filing may trigger formal tax audit and coercive collection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Final Beneficial Owner Return (Información de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before 31 July; exact transmission window set by DIAN annual resolution for the reporting year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate, late, or omitted data exposes the company to penalties under Articles 651 and 658-3 of the Tax Code, up to 13,600 UVT per infraction (approximately USD 159,000), and may impair tax compliance certification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Exogenous Third-Party Information Return (Información Exógena)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN - Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 June of the year following the reporting period, subject to the DIAN NIT-digit transmission calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or erroneous submission is penalized under Articles 641 and 651 of the Tax Code; maximum fine of 13,600 UVT (approximately USD 159,000) or 10% of omitted amounts when quantifiable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements Deposit (Depósito de Estados Financieros)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval at the ordinary shareholders' meeting; the ordinary meeting must be held on or before 31 March after the calendar year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-deposit prevents use of financial statements against third parties and may trigger administrative fines; prolonged default impedes registry renewal and may block lawful operations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary Shareholders' Meeting and Corporate Minutes (Asamblea de Accionistas)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company corporate minutes book registered at the Cámara de Comercio
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after fiscal year-end; for calendar-year S.A.S. entities no later than 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors and managing shareholders may be jointly liable for failure to approve financial statements; persistent noncompliance is a statutory cause for forced dissolution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory auditor (Revisor Fiscal) is mandatory when total assets exceed 5,000 SMLMV or gross revenues exceed 3,000 SMLMV at the prior year-end (approximately USD 1.9 million and USD 1.1 million, respectively); securities intermediaries, financial market participants, and high-frequency trading operators must appoint a Revisor Fiscal regardless of these thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Full IFRS / NIIF for Group 1 public-interest entities; IFRS for SMEs (NIIF para PYMES) for most S.A.S. proprietary trading companies; simplified micro-entity framework for Group 3; books and financial statements are maintained in COP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every shareholding or beneficial ownership change must be approved, recorded in the share register, and reported through the DIAN final beneficiary system within the applicable update window; an annual final beneficiary confirmation return must accompany the corporate compliance cycle. Share certificates, transfer minutes, and related supporting documents must be retained for statutory verification.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (Registro de la Junta Directiva / Representantes Legales)
Minute Book of Shareholders' Meetings (Actas de Asamblea de Accionistas)
Minute Book of Board or Sole Shareholder Resolutions (Actas de Junta Directiva / Decisiones del Accionista Único)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general corporate income tax holiday applies to proprietary algorithmic high-frequency trading. The Colombian SAS is taxed at 35% on worldwide net taxable income. Preferential regimes are limited and generally unavailable to trading income: (i) newly created cultural/creative 'orange economy' ventures may obtain a seven-year income tax exemption on qualifying software-related revenues, subject to prior DIAN registration, annual revenue caps, and net-employment requirements; (ii) taxpayers in authorized free trade zones may apply a 20% corporate income tax rate to qualifying activities. No statutory HFT-specific exemption exists.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 210 — Declaración de Renta y Complementario para Personas Jurídicas y Asimiladas; filed electronically through the DIAN MUISCA 'Sede Electrónica' portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Sociedades por Acciones Simplificadas are required to follow the calendar tax year. The annual corporate income tax return for the preceding calendar year is due on the date fixed by DIAN Resolution according to the last two digits of the taxpayer’s NIT, usually between the first working day of April and the last working day of September of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross operating revenues of the HFT proprietary trading business, including realized trading gains, market-making spreads, commissions, financing revenues, and exchange gains treated as ordinary trading income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident foreign trading entity without a Colombian permanent establishment does not file this form in respect of foreign-source HFT income. Where a Colombian PE exists, report only gross income economically connected to the PE. Colombian-source trading gains realized by a non-resident through a local broker may be subject to definitive withholding rather than a return obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Occasional income, periodic financial income, derivative gains outside the core trading book, revaluation adjustments, and other non-operating revenues.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders are not taxed on these items unless the income is Colombian-source or attributable to a Colombian PE. Colombian-source occasional gains are reportable and subject to the 15% occasional gains rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutorily exempt income; for the relevant entity, only a registered qualifying 'orange economy' exemption could be invoked, and only on revenues from qualifying software/creative activity with admissible evidence before DIAN.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident entity is not entitled to Colombian renta exenta unless the income is earned through a Colombian PE and the exemption is specifically admissible under the applicable law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Renglón 08 — Costos de venta y operación directa
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs attributable to trading operations: exchange clearing fees, market-data feeds, colocation and ultra-low-latency connectivity charges, hardware depreciation, and direct operational overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents without a Colombian PE cannot deduct such costs locally. For a Colombian PE, costs must be causally connected to PE income, supported by transfer pricing documentation when paid to related foreign entities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ordinary, necessary, and proportional deductions such as employee compensation, research and development amortization, software licenses, rent, insurance, professional fees, and financial expenses. Accrual basis is mandatory.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments made to non-resident related parties must satisfy the arm's length standard; otherwise deductions are disallowed or recharacterized. Payments subject to foreign withholding tax require documentary evidence of withholding and, where treaty relief is claimed, a valid Tax Residence Certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Occasional capital gains, particularly gains from disposal of assets not held as ordinary revenue assets, taxed at 15%. HFT portfolio positions that are continuously traded may instead be ordinary revenue assets; consistent classification is required.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Colombian-source occasional gains are reportable. Non-resident sellers of Colombian shares or assets are subject to the 15% rate through the purchaser or broker withholding mechanism when no PE exists.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty is 5% of the income tax due for each month or fraction of delay, capped at 100% of the tax due; where no tax is due, a fixed UVT-based penalty applies. Late filing after formal DIAN summons may increase the penalty by 10% per month. Interest accrues at the statutory moratorium rate, currently approximately one and a half times the central bank lending rate. In addition, inaccurate or false returns trigger the inexactitud penalty of 100% of the understated tax, and criminal tax evasion sanctions can apply where the concealed amount exceeds the statutory criminal threshold.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 120 — Informe Individual / Local File (Declaración Informativa de Precios de Transferencia) and Formulario 123 — Master File, if applicable; filed electronically through the same DIAN MUISCA 'Sede Electrónica' portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The transfer pricing informative return and documentation forms are due on the same statutory deadlines established for the annual corporate income tax return, based on the last two digits of the taxpayer's NIT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section A — Identification of related parties
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Complete identification, tax residence, relationship type, and intermediary role of each related counterparty, including foreign algorithm or market-making affiliates, group data centers, and colocation providers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident related parties must be identified with their foreign tax identification number and country of tax residence; TRC details must be provided where treaty relief or permanent establishment analysis is relevant.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section B — Intercompany transactions and amounts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate values of transactions with related parties by category: equity, debt, derivatives, market-data royalties, software license fees, colocation services, management services, risk-sharing arrangements, and guaranteed trading capacity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Transactions with non-resident related parties must be priced under the arm's length standard; each category must include the method used, selected comparables, and functional analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section C — Transfer pricing methodology and comparables
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detailed selection and justification of the tested party, comparable data, financial adjustments, and arm's-length range for each material transaction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Comparable analysis must reflect risks of high-frequency trading: algorithmic development, order-flow latency, market risk, counterparty credit risk, and operational continuity. Foreign comparables require adjustment for Colombian market conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Master File narrative of the multinational group’s business, organizational structure, intercompany financing, intangibles, and financial results; required only where the group’s consolidated revenue exceeds the applicable UVT threshold.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Master File must describe the foreign head office’s algorithmic IP ownership, R&D budget, IP registration, and the Colombian SAS’s substantive functions in operating the trading systems.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file or late filing of the transfer pricing documentation exposes the taxpayer to a penalty of 5% of the value of the related-party transactions, subject to a statutory UVT ceiling, plus the standard 5% monthly late-filing surcharge. DIAN may also reject the taxpayer’s transfer pricing position, reallocate income, and impose the general inexactitude penalty of 100% of the resulting tax deficiency.
